papers.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners (GPT-2)
papers.authors: Radford, Wu, Child, Luan, Amodei, Sutskever (OpenAI)
papers.hint: 1.5B decoder-only LM trained on WebText (40GB, outbound Reddit links). Zero-shot task transfer: no task-specific fine-tuning, just prompt. Introduced the 'language models are unsupervised multitask learners' thesis; byte-level BPE; famously staged release over misuse worries.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
papers.authors: Kaplan, McCandlish, Henighan, Brown, Chess, Child, Gray, Radford, Wu, Amodei (OpenAI)
papers.hint: Loss follows smooth power laws in model size N, dataset size D, and compute C over many orders of magnitude. L(N) ~ (Nc/N)^alpha etc. Bigger models are more sample-efficient; for a fixed compute budget, train very large models and stop before convergence. Predicts GPT-3. Later refined by Chinchilla.

papers.title: The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling
papers.hint: 825 GiB open pretraining corpus of 22 curated sub-datasets (PubMed, arXiv, GitHub, StackExchange, books, etc.). Deliberately diverse to improve generalization. Became the standard open pretraining set (GPT-Neo/J, Pythia). Introduced careful documentation of data provenance.

papers.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
papers.hint: 540B dense decoder trained on 6144 TPU v4 chips via the Pathways system. Breakthrough few-shot reasoning; chain-of-thought + PaLM cracks hard BIG-bench tasks; discontinuous 'emergent' jumps at scale. Architecture: SwiGLU, parallel layers, multi-query attention, RoPE, no biases.

papers.title: OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models
papers.authors: Zhang, Roller, Goyal, et al. (Meta AI)
papers.hint: Open reproduction of GPT-3 scale (125M-175B) with weights released to researchers. Notable for the released logbook documenting training instabilities (loss spikes, hardware failures, restarts) — a rare honest look at training a 175B model at ~1/7th GPT-3's carbon.

papers.title: BLOOM: A 176B-Parameter Open-Access Multilingual Language Model
papers.hint: 176B open multilingual model (46 natural + 13 programming languages) from the BigScience collaboration of 1000+ researchers. Trained on the ROOTS corpus on France's Jean Zay supercomputer. Emphasis on open governance, data ethics, and Responsible AI License.

papers.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
papers.authors: Touvron, Lavril, Izacard, et al. (Meta AI)
papers.hint: 7B-65B trained only on public data; LLaMA-13B beats GPT-3 175B on most benchmarks by training smaller models on far more tokens (1-1.4T), Chinchilla-style. Architecture: RMSNorm pre-norm, SwiGLU, RoPE. The weight leak seeded the entire open-LLM ecosystem (Alpaca, Vicuna...).

papers.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
papers.hint: Align a model with minimal human labels using a written 'constitution' (a list of principles). Two phases: (1) supervised — model critiques and revises its own harmful answers against the principles; (2) RLAIF — a model generates the preference labels for RL instead of humans. Basis of Claude's harmlessness training.

papers.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
papers.hint: Bootstrap instruction-tuning data from the model itself: seed with 175 human tasks, have the LM generate new instructions + instances, filter for quality/diversity, fine-tune on the result. Nearly matches InstructGPT with almost no human annotation. The recipe behind Alpaca.

papers.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE)
papers.authors: Su, Lu, Pan, Murtadha, Wen, Liu
papers.hint: Encode position by ROTATING each query/key vector by an angle proportional to its position. The dot product then depends only on relative position (m-n), giving relative-position awareness inside plain dot-product attention. Decays with distance; extrapolates; now standard in LLaMA/GPT-NeoX/PaLM/most modern LLMs.

papers.title: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases (ALiBi)
papers.hint: No position embeddings at all: just add a static, head-specific linear penalty -m*(distance) to each attention score, biasing toward recent tokens. Trains on short sequences yet extrapolates to much longer ones at inference. Simpler and cheaper than learned/sinusoidal positions.

papers.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need (Multi-Query Attention)
papers.hint: Share a SINGLE key/value head across all query heads. Shrinks the KV cache by a factor of the head count, so autoregressive decoding is memory-bandwidth bound far less — big inference speedup, small quality cost. Precursor to GQA; used in PaLM, Falcon.

papers.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
papers.hint: A small cheap 'draft' model proposes several tokens; the big target model verifies them all in ONE parallel forward pass and accepts the longest correct prefix (a provably distribution-preserving rejection-sampling scheme). 2-3x faster generation with identical output distribution.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.hint: Just prompt the model to show its reasoning steps ('let's think step by step' / few-shot exemplars with worked solutions) and multi-step reasoning improves dramatically. An emergent ability of scale (~100B). GSM8K math jumps massively. No fine-tuning; a prompting discovery that reframed how we use LLMs.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.authors: Yao, Zhao, Yu, Du, Shafran, Narasimhan, Cao
papers.hint: Interleave Thought -> Action -> Observation loops: the model reasons in language AND calls tools (search, APIs), feeding results back in. Reasoning guides which action to take; observations ground the reasoning, cutting hallucination. The template under most modern tool-using agents.

papers.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts
papers.hint: Two ideas for better MoE: (1) fine-grained experts — split each expert into many smaller ones for more combinations; (2) shared experts — a few always-on experts capture common knowledge so routed experts specialize. Matches larger models with far fewer active params; basis of DeepSeek-V2/V3.

papers.title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of LLMs
papers.hint: The KV cache dominates long-context memory. Observation: a small set of 'heavy-hitter' tokens account for most attention mass. H2O keeps recent tokens + heavy hitters and evicts the rest via a greedy policy, shrinking the KV cache up to ~5-10x with little accuracy loss.

papers.title: Muon: An Optimizer for the Hidden Layers of Neural Networks
papers.hint: Optimizer for 2D hidden weight matrices: take the momentum SGD update and ORTHOGONALIZE it (via a few Newton-Schulz iterations) before applying, so all singular directions get comparable step sizes. Faster wall-clock training than AdamW at scale; used in recent frontier training runs. Keep Adam for embeddings/heads.
